A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pol iota is a DNA polymerase that has evolved to replicate the Hoogsteen GxC and AxTx base pairs, which are the major base pairs in single-stranded DNA.

, unlike most other replicative DNA polymerases, Pol iota is able to form Hoogsteen base pairs in the active site and that the ability to form a Hoogsteen GxC base pair is critical for the high efficiency of correct nucleobase incorporation opposite template purine bases.

Pol iota has evolved to be a purine-specific polymerase, which is able to replicate through damaged templates by incorporating the correct nucleotides opposite template purines with high fidelity and opposite template pyrimidines with low fidelity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the template specificity exhibited by Pol iota is not due to a difference in the catalytic efficiency of correct nucleotides opposite purine or pyrimidine templates.

, although the Y family of polymerases, including Pol iota, can replicate through a variety of DNA structures that contain non-W-C base pairs, the fidelity of Pol iota is maintained by its ability to form Hoogsteen base pairs during normal DNA synthesis.
Pol iota is a unique polymerase that is capable of forming a Hoogsteen-type base pair with the templating residue and the incoming pyrimidyl nucleotide.
